prompt: Stage 3-2 augment round. At 2-1 you scouted three other players on your 2-cost reroll carry and decided to wait. Now, at 3-2, two of them are still holding the carry with a 2-star each, and you have a pair. You are level 5 with 44 gold at 78 HP, and your items are flexible AD components. Your board has a 2-star 3-cost AD carry from a different line. What is the play?

lobby.note: 2-star of your carry, holding 3 more copies on bench
2-star of your carry, AD items on it
Dropped the line, now on a tank vertical

options.label: Sell the pair, put the AD items on the 3-cost carry, and go up levels on the uncontested line
Roll down to 20 at level 5 to hit the 3-star before they do
Keep holding the pair to 4-1 and see if a third player drops

explanation:
One competitor holding five copies plus another 2-star means at least eight of the twenty-five copies are gone before you roll, and the two of them will keep buying. Your 3-star needs nine. That is not a race you win from a pair, and every roll at level 5 that misses is gold you needed for the 4-1 level. The read you postponed at 2-1 is now clear, and clear is the moment to act.

The pivot is cheap because your items are AD components and you already own a 2-star 3-cost AD carry with an item: nothing you sell was doing work. Waiting to 4-1 is the trap: you would spend stage 3 at level 5 with a 1-star carry on the board while the pool shrinks further and your HP pays for it.
principle: When the contest read becomes clear, pivot with gold in hand, not after a failed rolldown.
commonMistake: Rolling to prove you can hit. The pool does not care that you had the pair first.
